title: 2022 Knox Legal Studies Trial
notes: No answer key is included in the PDF; all answers are reasoned estimates. The Georgia scenario is shared by questions 2 and 3.

groups.stimulus: Georgia is the personal assistant of an international company based in Melbourne. She is charged with embezzling $250 000 from the company to buy a luxury car.

questions.stem: Selling alcohol to people under the age of 18 is an example of what type of crime?
questions.answerNote: Selling alcohol to minors is a strict liability offence.

questions.stem: The main factors affecting Georgia’s criminal behaviour are:
questions.answerNote: Embezzling to buy a luxury car is greed/self-interest rather than hardship; B (economic factors) is also plausible.

questions.stem: Georgia’s committal hearing will be heard in what court?
questions.answerNote: Committal proceedings are heard in the Local Court.

questions.stem: Where are trials for transnational crimes heard?
questions.answerNote: Transnational crimes are prosecuted under domestic jurisdiction.

questions.stem: The primary role of the Australian Federal Police is to enforce
questions.answerNote: The AFP primarily enforces Commonwealth law.

questions.stem: Under recent changes to the Bail Act a defendant must ‘show cause’ as part of the bail application. This may result in conflict with which of the following legal principles?
questions.answerNote: Requiring an accused to show cause may place pressure on the presumption of innocence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an expressed right under the Australian Constitution?
questions.answerNote: Freedom of religion is expressly protected by section 116.

questions.stem: Which of the following best ensures the protection of human rights in Australia?

options.A: Ratification of an international human rights treaty
options.B: A media investigation into human rights abuses occurring in Australia
options.C: Enactment of Federal human rights legislation
options.D: An Australian non-government organisation offering support to victims of human rights abuses

questions.answerNote: Domestic legislation gives rights direct legal effect in Australia.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements does NOT describe the role of non-government organisations (NGO’s) in protecting human rights?

options.A: NGO’s can assist victims of human rights abuses
options.B: NGO’s play a central role in enforcing human rights law
options.C: NGO’s use the media to name and shame human rights violators
options.D: NGO’s assist better compliance with human rights law by governments

questions.answerNote: NGOs promote compliance but do not centrally enforce human rights law.

questions.stem: At her sentencing hearing, Emily’s defence lawyer asks the judge to reduce the sentence because she is a young, single mother. This is an example of:
questions.answerNote: Personal circumstances may be considered as mitigating factors.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of forfeiture of assets as a punishment?

options.A: To remove the tainted proceeds of crime
options.B: To pay back the victims of crime
options.C: To force the offender to admit their guilt
options.D: To cover the costs of enforcement

questions.answerNote: Forfeiture removes the proceeds or instrumentalities of crime.

questions.stem: The Commonwealth decides to challenge new NSW legislation on immigration in the High Court. What principle is being tested?
questions.answerNote: A Commonwealth–state dispute tests the division of legislative powers.

questions.stem: An offender completes their 6 month jail sentence through weekend detention. What type of detention is this?
questions.answerNote: Weekend custody is periodic detention.

questions.stem: Extradition involves:

options.A: Charging a person with a transnational crime
options.B: Charging a person with the same crime in two locations
options.C: A person being prosecuted in the International Criminal Court
options.D: Returning a person to the jurisdiction in which they committed the crime

questions.answerNote: Extradition returns a person to the jurisdiction seeking prosecution.

questions.stem: A person must have a reasonable prospect of success in their case to be eligible for legal aid. Which of the following best describes this requirement?
questions.answerNote: The merit test assesses the prospects and public value of a case.

questions.stem: Benjamin organised a protest of angry government workers. He was arrested by the police. Which of the following human rights has Benjamin been denied?

options.B: The right to freedom of assembly
options.C: The right to join a trade union
options.D: The right to freedom and security of person

questions.answerNote: The scenario concerns peaceful assembly.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an alternative to court for a young offender?
questions.answerNote: A police caution diverts a young offender without court proceedings.

questions.stem: Which group of factors constitute post-sentencing decisions?

options.A: Protective custody, sexual offenders registration, parole
options.B: Security classification, parole, level of violence used
options.C: Parole, criminal record of the victim, sexual offenders registration
options.D: Security classification, preventative and continued detention, age of the victim

questions.answerNote: Protective custody, registration and parole are post-sentence matters.

questions.stem: An Australian is caught at an international airport in Asia, attempting to smuggle drugs back to Australia. Under which jurisdiction would the Australian be prosecuted?
questions.answerNote: The offence is prosecuted under the law of the country where it is detected.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the term ‘treaty’?

options.C: A written agreement between States governed by domestic law
options.D: A written agreement between States governed by international law

questions.answerNote: A treaty is a written agreement between states governed by international law.
